import pandas as pd
import seaborn as sns
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import io

# Load the dataset from the provided string
data = """survived,pclass,sex,age,sibsp,parch,fare,embarked,class,who,adult_male,deck,embark_town,alive,alone
0,3,male,22.0,1,0,7.25,S,Third,man,True,,Southampton,no,False
1,1,female,38.0,1,0,71.2833,C,First,woman,False,C,Cherbourg,yes,False
1,3,female,26.0,0,0,7.925,S,Third,woman,False,,Southampton,yes,True
1,1,female,35.0,1,0,53.1,S,First,woman,False,C,Southampton,yes,False
0,3,male,35.0,0,0,8.05,S,Third,man,True,,Southampton,no,True
"""
df = pd.read_csv(io.StringIO(data))

# Create a categorical plot to show survival rate by passenger class and sex
# 'survived' (0/1) as y will automatically calculate the mean (survival rate) for 'kind="bar"'
g = sns.catplot(
    data=df,
    x="pclass",
    y="survived",
    hue="sex",
    kind="bar",
    palette="viridis", # Choose a color palette
    height=5,            # Height of the plot
    aspect=1.2           # Aspect ratio of the plot
)

# Set descriptive titles and labels
g.set_axis_labels("Passenger Class", "Survival Rate")
g.fig.suptitle("Titanic Survival Rates by Passenger Class and Sex", y=1.03) # Main title

# Adjust layout to prevent labels from overlapping
plt.tight_layout()

# Save the plot to a file
plt.savefig("output.png")
